issues.p: Self-Retaining (Foley) 2-Way PTFE Coated Latex catheters, 12Ch to 22Ch (12 product codes)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3267, opened 24/02/2026 and last updated 09/07/2026, now marked Resolved and closed. issues.p: NephroMax high pressure nephrostomy balloon catheters (eight affected product codes)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain field safety notice (ICN 3416) dated 22/07/2026: the renal sheath on affected lots may be packaged in a reversed orientation, and if this is not corrected before use the non-tapered end may be inserted in the patient, which could increase resistance and result in difficulty advancing, withdrawing or positioning the catheter. The eight affected products remain available via eDirect; users are told to verify sheath orientation before use and correct it if necessary, as described in Appendix A of the notice. No alternative product is named.
issues.use: This is a check-before-use correction rather than a withdrawal, so there is no supply gap to fill here. It is still a fair reason to ask your urology and interventional radiology accounts whether the notice has reached the people actually opening the packs.

issues.p: Convatec EsteemBody one-piece intestinal ostomy bag, open-ended (MHRA ref 38578479)
issues.s: Field safety notice listed on the MHRA's 16-20 February 2026 FSN page (Convatec EsteemBody, one-piece intestinal ostomy bag, open-ended, ref 38578479); the listing does not state the nature of the issue - read the FSN itself before quoting it. issues.use: An open field safety notice on a one-piece ostomy bag is a reason to ask your stoma care accounts whether they hold EsteemBody stock and what they would move to, without assuming the fault.

issues.p: ChloraPrep 2% applicators and the procedure packs containing them: NPC codes DMK000 (1ml), MRB303 (1.5ml), MRB306 (3ml) and MRB494 (3ml tinted)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3359, latest update 28/07/2026: MHRA recall for a potential breach of sterility in the packaging process, expanded to all lot numbers with an expiry date up to and including 05/2029. Trusts are told to cease use and quarantine all affected products, and to return stocked items by Friday 14 August 2026 — except Rocialle stocked products, where the notice states 'All goods to be returned no later than Friday 7 August 2026' using reason code 7. Procedure packs from B Braun, Unisurge, Rocialle Healthcare and Kimal are also caught.
issues.use: The same sterility recall as ICN 3355, widened to the procedure packs that contain ChloraPrep. Every account that preps a line is quarantining stock and returning it, so ask what they are prepping with in the meantime and whether that stand-in is likely to stick. Check the deadline that actually applies to them: Rocialle stocked products are due back by 7 August 2026, everything else by 14 August 2026. Worth checking procedure-pack users too, not just applicator users. For what it has done to availability, see ICN 3397.

issues.p: Cannulation packs, 13 product codes (full list in the notice's attachment)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain notice 28/07/2026: all 13 affected codes are suspended and unavailable to order, caused by a component shortage and by the recall on ChloraPrep, which is a component in these packs. NHS Supply Chain states there are no alternatives available and anticipates the supply issue will be resolved by 31 August 2026.
issues.use: Thirteen B Braun cannulation pack codes are off the shelf until the end of August with no alternative listed, so ask cannulation accounts how they are covering the gap and whether your own pack or the individual components can fill it. This is a knock on from the ChloraPrep sterility recall in ICN 3359, which caught the applicators inside these packs, so treat the two as one conversation rather than two.

issues.p: DEC85019 — Prevantics skin disinfectant swabstick, 1.6ml, 2% chlorhexidine in 70% alcohol, 50 per pack
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3423, issued 03/08/2026 at 10:37. DEC85019 (‘Skin Disinfectant BIOCIDE 1.6ml swabstick 2% chlorhexidine in 70% alcohol 50 per pack’, brand Prevantics) is affected by ‘increased demand and lead times’. The code is still available to order but has been placed under Protect Demand Management, so ‘trusts are allocated a maximum daily quantity or “threshold”’. Potential indirect alternatives are mapped on the online catalogue. Resolution is anticipated by 31 October 2026.
issues.use: Read this alongside the ChloraPrep notices, not on its own. ‘Increased demand’ on a 2% chlorhexidine / 70% alcohol swabstick in the same fortnight the ChloraPrep applicators are recalled and rationed is the recall’s spill-over — and PDI’s anticipated resolution date, 31/10/2026, is the same date as ChloraPrep’s under ICN 3397. The two most obvious substitutes for each other are therefore capped at the same time, which is the thing a trust may not have joined up. Ask what their daily threshold actually is and whether it covers real usage rather than average usage. On alternatives, NHS Supply Chain’s Skin Disinfectant BIOCIDE section holds 32 codes and the 2% CHG / 70% alcohol set within it is short enough to name: PDI’s own Prevantics applicators (DEC85017 26ml, DEC85034 10.5ml), Cod Beck Blenders’ CoClens bottled solutions (DEC85002 500ml clear, DEC85023 200ml, DEC85027 200ml red staining ready-to-apply) and B Braun’s 500ml bottles (DEC85071 tinted, DEC85072 clear). Note what that list tells you: like-for-like single-use swabstick alternatives are thin, and most of what remains is a bottle, which is a different product with a different infection-control conversation attached. If you sell a single-use CHG/alcohol applicator, that gap is the pitch.

issues.co: B Braun, Baxter, Becton Dickinson UK Ltd, CODAN, Fannin, GBUK Group Ltd and RPG Medical Ltd
issues.p: IV infusion giving sets and blood transfusion giving sets
issues.s: MHRA Device Safety Information DSI/2026/003, issued 20/05/2026, prompted by a case in which an IV infusion giving set was used instead of a blood transfusion giving set during a neonatal exchange transfusion, causing cardiac arrest and severe brain injury. Using an IV set instead may under-infuse blood or destroy red blood cells (haemolysis). Required actions: store blood transfusion giving sets in clearly labelled containers, in their original packaging, separate from IV infusion giving sets; train staff to tell the two apart; complete a pre-transfusion checklist before starting.
issues.use: This is a storage, labelling and training alert, not a product fault or a recall, so there is no supply gap to sell into. It does open a legitimate conversation about how transfusion sets are stored and distinguished on the ward, and whether clearer packaging or separate storage helps the trust close the actions.

issues.p: balance 2.3% glucose, 1.25 mmol/l calcium, solution for peritoneal dialysis (PL 13689/0013)
issues.s: Class 4 Medicines Defect Notification (DMRC 39439934), issued 14/05/2026: the Braille text on the outer labels incorrectly states 'CAPD/DPCA 19' rather than the correct glucose and calcium composition. Six batches are affected: F4LM071, G4LB133, G4LL144, G4LM152, H4LB212 and G4LI151. The MHRA states there is no product quality issue, the affected batches will not be recalled, and patients may continue to use them. Healthcare professionals should explain the error to visually impaired patients who rely solely on Braille.
issues.use: Low impact and no switching opening: nothing is being recalled and there is no supply gap. It is a fair reason to check in with renal units, who have to flag the Braille error to visually impaired patients themselves.

issues.p: KFK036 — BD Vacutainer blood collection multi-sampling adaptor
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3385, opened 24/06/2026 and last updated 03/08/2026. KFK036 (‘Blood Collection Support Product Adaptor multi sampling’, brand Vacutainer) is affected by ‘supplier manufacturing issues’ and ‘remains subject to Protect Demand Management’, with trusts allocated ‘a maximum daily quantity or “threshold”’. Three alternatives are named in the notice: KFK232 (Adaptor Luer multisampling 20g), KFK978 (Adaptor Sampling Luer) and FNG85289 (Holder Multi-sampling Luer Adaptor). NHS Supply Chain advises that ‘due to the clinical nature of these alternative products, we advise you to consult your own clinical experts to ensure suitability for your organisations use’. Resolution is anticipated by 17 September 2026.
issues.use: The key facts first, because this is a category where the competitor set is unusually knowable. Blood collection sits on NHS Supply Chain’s Blood Collection Devices framework, which started 13 October 2025 and expires 12 October 2027 with an option to extend by 24 months. It is a single lot carrying 19 awarded suppliers, nine of them new to it: Balmung Medical Handel, Becton Dickinson U.K., Cambridge Sensors, Crest Medical, GBUK, Greiner Bio-One, Iskus Health UK, ISOL8 Healthcare, Nipro Medical Europe, Owen Mumford, Prosum Medical, Radiometer, Reflex Medical, Reliance Medical, RPG Medical, Sarstedt, Siemens Healthcare Diagnostics, Smiths Medical International and Vygon (UK). It replaced and combined the former Blood Collection Systems and Blood Lancets and Blood Culture Collection Systems frameworks, so a trust’s incumbent may be on it under a different arrangement than the one they remember. ·· Now the specific opening. The multi-sampling adaptor section of the catalogue holds only seven codes, and the three the notice names as alternatives to BD’s KFK036 belong to three different competitors: KFK232 is Greiner Bio-One’s Vacuette, KFK978 is GBUK Healthcare’s Prosum and FNG85289 is Crest Medical’s SOL-M. The rest of the section is Sarstedt — S-Monovette (KCM096, KCM114, KCM128) plus FNG85313. So a trust capped on KFK036 has four suppliers it can realistically move to, and NHS Supply Chain has already told it to take clinical advice before it does. Somebody has to have that clinical conversation, and it may as well be you. ·· Sarstedt is the one worth understanding, because S-Monovette is not a like-for-like swap. Sarstedt’s own product page describes it working by aspiration — ‘the plunger rod is gently pulled’, so ‘blood flow can be adapted to the patient’s vein conditions and vein collapse can be avoided’ — as well as by vacuum. Moving to it changes technique and training, not just a code. Greiner’s Vacuette and Crest’s SOL-M are the closer swaps. Ask which of the four they have actually validated, whether the threshold is biting in phlebotomy or on the wards, and — the question most reps miss — who owns the decision, because blood collection sits with pathology and phlebotomy, not with the vascular access team you may already know. ·· That last point is the link worth making. Blood collection is nested under Vascular access here because the same accounts touch both, but the buyer is not the same person. If you already hold the vascular access relationship, this notice is a warm route into pathology through a colleague who already trusts you. Resolution is anticipated 17 September 2026, so the window is real but it is not long.

issues.p: Nitrile examination gloves — contractual change (ICN 3425)
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3425, issued 03/08/2026 at 16:01 and categorised by NHS Supply Chain as a pricing update. The open notice says only: ‘We have been informed of a contractual change on nitrile examination gloves.’ The affected NPC codes and the nature of the change sit in a login-gated PDF in the Downloads section (‘3425 Polyco Healthline Nitrile Examination Gloves Contractual Change Notification 3 August 2026’), so neither the codes nor the direction of any price movement can be verified from outside NHS Supply Chain. No deadline or resolution date is published on the open page.
issues.use: Do not guess at this one in front of a customer. What is verifiable from outside is the fact of a contractual change on nitrile examination gloves and the date it was issued — the codes and the actual change are behind an NHS Supply Chain login, and inventing a direction of travel for a glove price is how a rep loses a procurement contact. Use it as a reason to ask rather than a fact to assert: your procurement and infection prevention contacts can open that PDF, so ask them what it says and which of their codes it touches. Gloves are a volume line, so even a small unit change shows up as a visible number on a trust’s spend, and being the person who flagged it before the invoice landed is worth more here than any product point. If it turns out to affect codes you compete on, come back to it then — with the notice open on the screen.
issues.gated: The product codes and the change itself are in a login-gated PDF on NHS Supply Chain. Nothing beyond the fact and date of the change can be verified from outside.

issues.p: Dräger Atlan anaesthesia workstations — risk of piston ventilator failure (DSI/2026/005)
issues.s: MHRA Device Safety Information DSI/2026/005, issued 04/08/2026, widening the scope of an October 2024 field safety notice. A manufacturing defect in the ventilator motor assembly may cause piston ventilator failure before or during use. The MHRA states: ‘Interruption in the ventilation of a patient could lead to hypoxia and potentially death if not recognised and managed promptly.’ If it fails in use the workstation displays ‘Ventilator error!!!!’ with an acoustic alarm, and manual/spontaneous ventilation and monitoring functions remain available. Required actions: check against the FSN whether your devices are affected; ensure Dräger replaces the motor assembly in all affected units; until that is done, affected devices ‘can continue to be used only with permanent supervision’, with staff briefed on manual ventilation and local protocol; distribute the FSN to all users and return the reply card to your Dräger representative. As at 29/07/2026 no confirmed patient injuries or deaths had been reported.
issues.use: Two angles here, and they are different jobs. If you are a competitor: this is not a supply gap and not a switching pitch, so do not run at it as one. What it does create is a supervision burden — every affected Atlan stays in service ‘only with permanent supervision’ until Dräger has swapped the motor assembly, which ties trained hands to a theatre list. Ask your anaesthetic and theatre accounts how many of their workstations are on the list, where they sit in the replacement queue, and what the supervision condition is doing to their list planning. That is a capacity conversation, and capacity is where a value case lives. If you work for Dräger — or for any company carrying an open alert of its own — this is the model worth copying: get to the customer before the alert does, tell them which of their units are affected and where they are in the queue, and hand them the briefing sheet for their staff. An issue handled openly buys more trust than a clean record nobody noticed. Whichever side you are on, cite the alert itself (DSI/2026/005 on gov.uk) rather than paraphrasing it, and quote the MHRA’s own wording on the risk and on the supervision condition. An anaesthetist will know this alert better than you do, and being caught rounding it up ends the meeting.

issues.p: FDK317 and FDK049 — Skintact® automated defibrillation electrodes for Zoll defibrillators
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3426, issued 04/08/2026. Field safety notice from Fannin (UK) Ltd covering FDK317 (automated defibrillation pair, adult, 140 x 115mm, for use with Zoll defibrillators) and FDK049 (automated defibrillation paediatric multifunction electrode, 117 x 80mm, for Zoll defibrillators up to 25kg), manufactured by Leonhard Lang GmbH. On affected stock the connector cannot be fully inserted into the compatible adapter cable with normal force: ‘the locking tab does not engage and the auditable “click” is absent’. The manufacturer confirms electrical contact and retention still meet requirements and that ‘safety and performance are not impaired’. NHS Supply Chain records that this is ‘not a product withdrawal or recall’ and that no further action is required beyond reading the FSN and sharing it with all users. Incoming FDK317 stock will be placed under Control Demand Management and customers ordering it will receive affected stock, with unaffected stock expected end of August 2026.
issues.use: No recall and no supply gap, so lead with the practice question rather than the product. The missing click is the whole issue: a defibrillation pad that seats without its confirmation click is a confidence problem in an arrest even when the manufacturer says performance is unaffected. Ask what resus leads and practice educators are hearing from staff who have applied one, whether it has changed how they check placement, and whether it has come up in a resus debrief. Then help them close it — the fix here is a briefing to users, not a switch. If you do sell into this, Lot 8 (Defibrillation Electrodes and Pads) of the Electrodes, Ultrasound Gels, Defibrillation and Related Consumables framework runs 01/02/2024 to 31/01/2028 and carries 37 awarded suppliers, Fannin among them. The direct alternatives for Zoll-fit pads on the catalogue are Zoll Medical UK’s own (FBH85027 adult and FBH85028 paediatric multifunction electrodes for AED Plus / R Series / X Series, FDJ1736 and FDJ1737 OneStep), ConMed’s PadPro with a Zoll connector (FDJ85057) and Telic via Surgical Holdings (FDJ85071, Zoll-M&B paediatric); Stryker, Ambu, Philips, Mindray, Schiller, GE Medical and Nissha are also on the lot. Stay off the fear angle. The notice itself says safety and performance are not impaired, and a rep who overstates it will be corrected by the FSN in the room.

issues.p: FDK6925 and FDK6926 — AirLife volume incentive spirometers, 4000ml and 2500ml
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3179, opened 09/12/2025 and last updated 03/08/2026 — its thirteenth update. Two codes are suspended and unavailable to order: FDK6925 (‘Spirometer volume incentive 4000ml without one-way valve 12/cs NON RETURNABLE’) and FDK6926 (the 2500ml version). The notice gives the cause as ‘raw material shortage’ and anticipates resolution by 10 August 2026. For FDK6925 ‘potential indirect alternative products are available to order through our online catalogue’, with the caution that those alternatives ‘may also become subject to intermittent supply with the increase in demand’; no alternatives are available for FDK6926. Filed here under Respiratory rather than Vascular access: NHS Supply Chain’s own page title reads ‘Nasal Cannula and Oxygen Facemask Products’, and across eight months this notice has moved over spirometers, gas sampling lines, nasal cannulae and oxygen facemasks — every product family it has covered is respiratory, none is vascular access.
issues.use: Incentive spirometry is post-operative and respiratory-ward business, and it is the ward that feels this rather than procurement. Both AirLife volume incentive codes are off the shelf and FDK6926 has no alternative listed at all — and on NHS Supply Chain’s own catalogue these two are the only volume incentive spirometers in the Spirometer section; the other six codes in it are Dräger flow sensors and waterlocks. That is the opening: a trust with no listed alternative is the one buyer with a reason to look outside the catalogue today, so if your range includes a volume incentive spirometer, this is the week to say so. Handle the resolution date carefully. It says 10 August 2026, but the notice has been running since 09/12/2025 across thirteen updates and the date has moved repeatedly, so ask what they have actually been able to get in the last month rather than what the notice promises. Physiotherapy and enhanced-recovery leads will know before procurement does.

dates.note: date has moved repeatedly since 09/12/2025 — treat as indicative

issues.reclassified: Moved from vascular to respiratory on 05/08/2026: every product family this notice has covered is respiratory. Flagged as a suspected false positive under Vascular access on 04/08/2026; reclassified rather than deleted, because the notice itself is real.

issues.p: FAB85002, FWM4155, FWM4157, FWM85015, FWM85047, FWM85062 and FWM85131 - NGPOD enteral feeding device accessories and pH reading device

issues.p: Palacos and Copal bone cement — 15 codes suspended, 5 still available
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3261, opened 17/02/2026 and last updated 05/08/2026. Heraeus Medical “encountered a packaging fault which temporarily stopped production of their pouch bone cement products”, later traced to a technical machine failure. Nine codes are suspended with availability estimated September 2026 (FQQ388, FJI4643, FQQ1101, FQQ1061, FQQ1151, FQQ1131, FQQ1091, FQQ1031, FQT85049) and six more are suspended with no expected date at all (FQQ113, FJT30864, FJT30863, FQQ1071, FQQ1161, FQQ1041). Five remain available: FQQ1001, FQQ1111, FQQ1081, FQQ1011, FQQ1021. NHS Supply Chain states that “while supply is improving, product availability has not yet returned to normal levels” and that trusts should “maintain a resilient supply position”; Heraeus is allocating roughly two weeks’ stock on historic ordering patterns. Three alternatives are named with codes: Zimmer Biomet Hi Fatigue G (FQT85055, FQT85054), Johnson & Johnson CMW Smartset GHV Gentamicin (FQT85035) and Tecres Vancogenx Dual Antibiotic HV via Summit Medical (FQT85014).
issues.use: The largest open supply gap in this feed, and the one with the clearest commercial shape. Fifteen bone cement codes are off the shelf, six of them with no return date, and NHS Supply Chain has already named three alternatives with catalogue codes against them — so the switching conversation is not hypothetical, it is written down. If you sell any of the three, the opening is simply to ask which of the fifteen an account still has on its preference card and whether theatres have validated a stand-in yet. If you sell none of them, this is still worth knowing: cement choice is surgeon preference and rarely reopens, so a trust forced onto an alternative for six months is a trust whose preference card is genuinely in play for the first time in years. Ask what they have actually been able to get, not what the notice lists — allocations are running at about two weeks of historic usage, so a busy arthroplasty list may be short even on the codes marked available.

dates.note: “September 2026” — no exact day given; six further codes have no date at all

issues.p: Biogel Super-Sensitive surgeons’ gloves — 975 range discontinued, replaced by 825
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3334, issued 18/05/2026 and marked Resolved at the 04/08/2026 update. The Biogel Super-Sensitive 975 range is discontinued and replaced by the 825 range across eight codes (FTE1755, FTE785, FTE786, FTE787, FTE788, FTE789, FTE790, FTE1756 — latex, powder-free, enhanced sensitivity, sterile pairs). The replacement has curved formers, “slightly thinner material to support tactile sensitivity and dexterity” and a smooth rather than textured surface, so it has less grip. Manufacturer product codes change; National Product Codes and pricing stay the same. FTE785, FTE787 and FTE790 ran out by mid-May 2026, and the notice states “no further stock of the Biogel Super-Sensitive 975 range will be supplied”.
issues.use: A product change dressed as an administrative update, and the detail is the opening: same NPC, same price, but a smooth surface instead of a textured one and thinner material. Surgeons notice grip. Every theatre still ordering these eight codes has already been moved without choosing to, so ask scrub teams and surgeons how the 825 is handling rather than whether they know about the change. Where grip is the complaint, that is a live reason to trial an alternative surgical glove — there are only nine suppliers on the Surgical Gloves framework, so the field is small and nameable. Do not oversell it: it is a range refresh, not a fault.

issues.p: FDJ2429 — standard blade electrode, disposable, Insulated EDGE Coated 2.75in
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3428, issued 05/08/2026. FDJ2429 (“Standard blade electrode disposable Insulated EDGE Coated 2.75inch”) is “currently suspended and unavailable to order” because of a component shortage. One alternative is named: FDJ3248, standard blade electrode disposable (E-Z CLEAN MOD 2.75IN). Resolution is anticipated by 30 September 2026. NHS Supply Chain advises consulting clinical experts on the alternative’s suitability and warns that alternatives may themselves become disrupted.
issues.use: New today and completely unavailable, not merely rationed, with a single named alternative. Electrosurgical tips are a per-case consumable, so a theatre gets to the end of its box quickly — this is a this-week conversation, not a next-quarter one. Ask theatre managers and the sterile services lead what they have on the shelf and whether FDJ3248 has been accepted by surgeons, because a coated insulated blade and an E-Z Clean blade do not behave identically in use. If you supply electrosurgical accessories, an eight-week gap on a Medtronic line is as clean an opening as this category offers.

issues.p: Forced air warming blankets — FDB85434–FDB85439 and VCB154
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3093, opened 17/09/2025 and last updated 17/07/2026 — nearly a year old and still open. FDB85435, FDB85438 and FDB85437 are available to order. FDB85436 (large paediatric underbody) is under Protect Demand Management with allocation thresholds. FDB85439 and FDB85434 are not yet available. VCB154 is available while stocks last and is being delisted. The original shortage came from reduced manufacturing capability caused by warehousing constraints; the supplier has since redesigned its speciality blanket range and introduced new codes to replace discontinued models. NHS Supply Chain will provide a further update by 14 August 2026.
issues.use: Perioperative normothermia is a measured standard, not a preference, so a warming blanket gap is a governance problem as well as a stock problem — that is the level to pitch this at. Note what is really happening: this is not just a shortage, it is a range redesign with new codes replacing discontinued ones, so a trust may be re-choosing rather than re-ordering. The paediatric underbody blanket is the pinch point, capped by threshold. Ask theatre and anaesthetic leads which codes they are actually receiving and whether the redesigned range has been evaluated, and watch for the update due 14 August.

issues.p: KTH110 — microscope slide, 76mm x 26mm, frosted end
issues.s: NHS Supply Chain ICN 3343, opened 28/05/2026 and last updated 04/08/2026. KTH110 (“Microscope Slide 76mm x 26mm 1-1.2mm thick 20mm Frosted End”) is “currently suspended and unavailable to order” because of “increased demand and lead times”. Three alternatives are named: KCP85099 (pink rather than frosted), KCP85101 and KCP85111 (both with 90-degree corners). Resolution is anticipated by 31 August 2026. NHS Supply Chain advises consulting clinical experts on suitability.
issues.use: Not glamorous, and that is the point — histopathology runs on consumables nobody discusses until they run out, and a frosted-end slide is where the specimen is labelled by hand. All three named alternatives differ physically from the original: one changes the writing surface from frosted to pink, two change the corners. Those differences matter to a lab that has automated staining or coverslipping calibrated around a slide, so “there is an alternative” is not the same as “there is no problem”. Ask the histopathology lab manager which alternative they have validated and whether it runs through their processor cleanly. Pathology is bought through its own framework and its own people; if you have never sold into a lab, this notice is a reason to be introduced.

clusters.title: Chlorhexidine and ChloraPrep — one running story, not eight notices
clusters.blurb: A sterility recall on ChloraPrep applicators has pulled in the procedure packs that contain them, the cannulation packs built around them and the nearest substitute swabstick. It is the biggest cluster in this feed and it owns the two nearest deadlines, so it is pinned here rather than left to be read one notice at a time. Treat it as one conversation: ask what an account is prepping with today, whether the stand-in is likely to stick, and which return deadline actually applies to them.
clusters.rule: Membership rule: every open notice in this feed whose affected product is a chlorhexidine skin preparation, or a pack containing one. 8 notices, all now under Skin prep and antisepsis — until 05/08/2026 five of them sat in a separate “Matched to a tracked product” bucket, which is why this thread used to read as two specialities. Nothing is inferred: each notice is listed above with its own source, and this panel holds no facts of its own.
